skill.name: project-structure
skill.desc: Directory layout, worktrees, ll.xml configuration, and document types.
skill.overview:
Development is organized under dev roots containing projects grouped by type. Each project has a git repository (`main/`) with optional worktrees for parallel development. Projects are configured via `ll.xml` manifests that Saddle discovers and uses for compilation.
This skill defines the physical layout and the document types used in software development: ``, ``, ``, and ``.
skill.dev_root:
A dev root is a directory containing project categories:
``` ~/dev/ ├── apps/ # Full applications ├── libs/ # Shared libraries ├── rust/ # Rust-specific projects └── kernel/ # Personal LLXML kernel ```
Saddle scans configured dev roots for `ll.xml` manifests.
skill.project_layout: ``` / # Operate from here ├── ll.xml # Project manifest and config ├── main/ # THE git repository (has .git/) ├── stable/ # Stable branch worktree (for vendoring) ├── _feature-x/ # Feature worktrees (underscore prefix) └── META/ # Dev-time, shared across worktrees ├── spec/ # Architecture specs (, ) ├── skills/ # Project-specific skills (dev-time, not shipped) ├── profiles/ # Saddle compilation profiles ├── inbox/ # Forward-looking items ├── retro/ # Backward-looking reflection ├── ctx/ # Compiled output (build artifact) ├── tickets/ # Ticket workflow directories │ ├── todo/ │ ├── in-progress/ │ ├── review/ │ └── done/ ├── logs/ # Development logs ├── remotes/ # Remote kernel skills ├── spikes/ # Research spikes ├── ref/ # External reference material └── archive/ # Old inbox/retro items ├── inbox/ └── retro/ ```
skill.ll_xml:
The `ll.xml` file is the project manifest and Saddle configuration point.
```xml
What this project is
```
```xml
Personal LLXML kernel
main/skills/
META/profiles/
META/inbox/
META/retro/
META/ctx/
META/tickets/
```
- `name` - Project identifier, used in frontmatter references - `v` - Version number - `skills global="true"` - This project contributes skills to global resolution - All paths relative to project root (where ll.xml lives)
Saddle discovers projects by scanning dev roots for ll.xml files. Multiple projects can contribute global skills (personal kernel, team shared, etc.).
Two places for skills:
- `main/skills/` - Global/shared skills that ship with the project. Used when `skills global="true"` in ll.xml. These are vendorable. - `META/skills/` - Project-specific skills for dev-time only. Not shipped, not vendored.
The kernel uses `main/skills/` because its skills are meant to be shared globally. Most apps use `META/skills/` for project-specific workflows.
skill.ctx:
The `META/ctx/` directory holds compiled context - build artifacts generated by Saddle.
**What it is:** - Compiled XML files ready for LLM consumption - Generated from profiles + selected items - Regenerated automatically on file changes
**What it is NOT:** - Hand-written context files - Source of truth (profiles are)
**How it works:** 1. User selects inbox/retro items in Saddle 2. User selects a profile 3. Saddle compiles: resolves includes, executes queries, assembles sections 4. Output written to `META/ctx/{profile}.xml` 5. LLM reads the compiled CTX to start session
Common compiled outputs: - `kickoff.xml` - Session start with inbox items - `reflection.xml` - Retro review - `ticket-work.xml` - Active ticket context
skill.profiles:
Profiles define what gets compiled into a CTX file. They live in `META/profiles/`.
```xml
Session start context
base
META/spec/app.xml inbox-workflow
task
```
Profiles support inheritance via `includes`, static file/skill references, and dynamic queries resolved at compile time.

skill.worktrees:
Git worktrees allow multiple working directories from a single repository.
- `main/` is the **actual git repository** (contains `.git/`) - Worktrees (`_feature-x/`) are lightweight checkouts referencing `main/.git` - Worktrees are ephemeral - created for tickets, removed after merge - `main/` is permanent - worktrees depend on it
From project root: ```bash cd main && git worktree add ../_{name} -b {name} ``` Creates branch `{name}` and directory `_{name}/` with that branch checked out.
After merge: ```bash git worktree remove _{name} ```
skill.vendoring:
Libraries share code via stable branches:
```bash git submodule add file:///stable vendor/ ```
"Publishing" = merging main to stable. Consumers get a snapshot via submodule.
See vendor-submodules skill for full details.
skill.key_concepts: - **ll.xml is config** - Project manifest, Saddle configuration point - **main/ is the repo** - Contains `.git/`, source of truth - **META/ is dev-time** - Not in git, shared across worktrees - **ctx/ is compiled** - Build artifact, not hand-written - **Worktrees are ephemeral** - Created for features, removed after merge - **Operate from project root** - Not from inside main/ or worktrees
skill.naming_conventions: - Project root: `~/dev///` - Git repository: `/main/` - Stable branch: `stable` - Feature worktrees: `/_feature-name/` - Vendor submodule: `main/vendor//` - Profiles: `META/profiles/.xml` - Compiled context: `META/ctx/.xml`
